name: Azure Pipelines

modes.label: Microsoft-hosted parallel jobs ($40 each/month, unlimited minutes)
modes.note: CI runner. Added 2026-09-28 (missing-providers audit). https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/devops/azure-devops-services/: additional Microsoft-hosted parallel job $40/month, unlimited minutes (job max 6 h on paid). Each agent = Standard_DS2_v2, 2 cores / 7 GB RAM / 14 GB SSD (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/pipelines/agents/hosted); no bigger machines. Priced as a flat pool of N parallel jobs = peak concurrency.

modes.label: Microsoft-hosted macOS parallel jobs ($40 each/month, unlimited minutes)
modes.note: Same $40 parallel job as Linux/Windows (the job pool is shared across OSes). macOS agents are Intel Mac 3-core / 14 GB / 14 GB SSD and always run in the US. 6 h job cap.

modes.label: GitHub-hosted agents (pay-as-you-go per minute, macOS arm64, preview)
modes.note: $0.062/min and $0.102/min; no free tier; no parallel job required; preview limit of 8 Standard + 8 XLarge agents per org; US only; same infrastructure as GitHub Actions larger runners. Per-minute rounding assumed (retail meter unit '1/Minute').

modes.label: Managed DevOps Pools (your Azure VMs + $15 self-hosted parallel job)
modes.note: Cost = standard Azure VM/disk/egress rates for the chosen VM size (see azure-vm card), plus $15/month per self-hosted parallel job beyond the 1 free. Standby agents are billed as VM hours even when idle. Azure Hybrid Benefit is not allowed. Lets you use any VM size (lifts the 2 vCPU/7 GB limit).

plans.name: Basic
plans.note: Pipelines itself has no per-user charge ('There's no per-user charge for using Azure Pipelines'); Basic user licences ($6/user/month after 5 free) are only needed for Repos/Boards. Free grant: 1 Microsoft-hosted job (60-min jobs, 1,800 min/month) + 1 self-hosted job (unlimited), private projects. The hosted free tier is not automatic: you must enable it by linking an Azure subscription (set up billing). No request form is mentioned anymore. Not encoded (engine cannot cap minutes). Public projects are retired and convert to private in 2027.

perf_source: No benchmark row: provider is not in ComputeSDK results or the HPC run (as of 2026-09-28). See research/perf-map.json.
caveats: Flat $40 per parallel job per month regardless of minutes; the engine sizes the pool by peak concurrency.
Free grant (1 hosted job, 1,800 min/month) not encoded.
Hosted Linux agents are fixed 2 vCPU / 7 GB; workloads needing more cannot be priced here (self-hosted/scale-set agents: $15 per self-hosted parallel job + your own VMs).
Windows/macOS hosted agents use the same parallel-job price but modes are Linux-only here.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

fleet.tiers: Free tier: 1 hosted job (60-min jobs, 1,800 min/month) after billing setup; paid: up to 25 hosted parallel jobs for new orgs
fleet.notes: Limit increases subject to regional capacity. GitHub-hosted (PAYG, preview) agents: 8 Standard + 8 XLarge per org; more via support case.

snapshot_auto.quote: Microsoft-hosted agents are run in individual VMs, which are reimaged after each run.
snapshot_auto.note: Job-scoped ephemeral CI VMs; nothing is saved at job end. Managed DevOps Pools 'Stateful' agents can be reused across jobs up to a max lifetime (e.g. 7 days) - agent reuse, not a snapshot.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Microsoft-hosted agents are run in individual VMs, which are reimaged after each run.
snapshot_on_demand.note: No snapshot/checkpoint API for hosted agents or Managed DevOps Pools agents in the docs; state reuse is via pipeline caching/artifacts.

harness_api.note: CI job runner; no first-party API to drive an agent harness inside the agent VM (only pipeline runs/REST API for pipelines). Not stated explicitly.

egress_allowlist.quote: You want to network isolate your CI/CD infrastructure by bringing your own virtual network with company-specific firewall rules.
egress_allowlist.note: Only for Managed DevOps Pools injected into your own Azure VNet, where Azure NSGs (IP/port) and Azure Firewall (FQDN) restrict outbound traffic; docs list endpoints to allowlist when 'network security groups or firewalls ... restrict outbound connectivity'. Microsoft-hosted agents: no egress controls (only published IP ranges to allowlist on your side).

ingress_rules.quote: By default, all pools use a Microsoft-provided virtual network, which restricts all inbound traffic and has the following outbound traffic configuration options.
ingress_rules.note: MDP: default VNet blocks all inbound; BYO VNet uses your NSG rules. Microsoft-hosted agents cannot expose ports at all: 'they aren't assigned public IP addresses. So, external entities can't target Microsoft-hosted agents.' No preview URLs.

guest_firewall.note: Hosted agents are full Azure VMs (Standard_DS2_v2) and 'Run as an administrator on Windows and a passwordless sudo user on Linux', so iptables/nftables should work; not documented explicitly.

secret_proxy.quote: To reference secret variables in YAML pipelines, map them as environment variables.
secret_proxy.note: Secrets (secret variables, variable groups/Key Vault, service connections) are decrypted onto the agent and masked in logs; no injecting egress proxy.

volume_attach.quote: Managed DevOps Pools supports attaching an empty data disk to the agents in your pool.
volume_attach.note: MDP only: one empty Azure managed data disk config per pool, attached to every agent; lives as long as the agent (stateless agents discarded per job). Microsoft-hosted agents: fixed ~10 GB free disk, 'We can't honor requests to increase disk space'.
